description: [LLM-Judge] Both control and attack SAML ACS posts returned HTTP 200/success but no authenticated session token was obtained, making the reported 'success' potentially a false positive and preventing verification of whether an unsigned Assertion was actually accepted.

sequence_description: Obtain an OAuth access token via password login, verify it is active, revoke it, then ensure it becomes inactive and cannot be used for UserInfo. Tests anti-replay after explicit revocation.

sequence_description: Password-login as userA to obtain a token, revoke it, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange using the revoked token as subject_token. Exchange should fail; success indicates revoked artifacts remain usable (replay after revocation). Includes userB as a second identity control.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token introspection returned an entity/user id even though the token was inactive and the preceding password grant failed, suggesting possible token/identity mix-up or introspection leakage.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token introspection returned an entity/user id even though the token was inactive and the preceding password grant failed, suggesting possible token/identity mix-up or introspection leakage.

sequence_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay after explicit session revocation: perform SAML login with <OneTimeUse/>, revoke the resulting OAuth session token, then attempt to reuse the exact same SAML Assertion/@ID again. Second acceptance indicates missing OneTimeUse/assertion replay enforcement independent of local session state.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML OneTimeUse replay attempt returned HTTP 200 (apparent acceptance), but the test cannot confirm a successful authenticated session because no session token/claims were obtained after the replay.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay attempt returned HTTP 200 (apparent acceptance), but the test cannot confirm a successful authenticated session because no session token/claims were obtained after the replay.
